data.title: Intel wins multiple upgrades on SA after earnings-led selloff
data.description:
Intel (INTC) fell more than 28% on Friday after its Q3 2026 results, as the semiconductor giant issued an underwhelming outlook for the current quarter, prompting multiple analysts to upgrade the stock on Seeking Alpha.

The selloff, Intel’s (INTC) biggest since the 1970s, is a key buying opportunity, argued SA analyst Mike Zaccardi based on a technical analysis. “INTC remains higher by 87% for 2026, and the current plunge appears as a key technical buying opportunity in my eyes,” wrote Zaccardi as he upgraded the stock to Buy from Sell.

Analyst Bohdan Kucheriavyi upgraded Intel (INTC), noting that the company’s earnings report “was quite decent” given its topline growth of ~21% and the earnings beat of $0.12 per share on an adjusted basis. “The issue, though, is that Q4 is expected to be a much weaker quarter in comparison to Q3," the analyst wrote as they upgraded the stock to Hold from Sell.

Analyst Kenio Fontes’ upgrade was based on the stock's improved margin of safety following the selloff. “Now I’m comfortable enough to upgrade Intel to a Hold. Yet, I’m not seeing enough margin of safety to be bullish about the stock,” Fontes added as he upgraded INTC to Hold from Sell.

The Asian Investor also issued a similar upgrade, arguing that Intel’s (INTC) valuation “has normalized” after the selloff, as the stock currently trades 50% lower than its year-ago level. “With Intel’s shares down ~50% from their 1-year high at ~$142, the valuation has returned closer to the chipmaker's historical average,” the analyst wrote.

However, Seeking Alpha Investing Group Leader Quad 7 Capital downgraded INTC to Sell from Hold, noting that the stock continues to trade at a level where “perfection is fully priced in, yet the forward picture is starting to show that high expectations are not being met.” “With full-year CapEx remaining heavy and Q4 earnings power decelerating rapidly, the stock's elevated premium looks increasingly unsustainable,” Quad 7 Capital argued.

data.title: Earnings Scorecard: 11 of 17 real estate companies beat revenue estimates this week
data.description:
With the earnings season picking pace, 17 companies in the State Street Real Estate Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLRE) reported quarterly results this week, with a majority beating revenue and EPS estimates.

Of the 17 firms, revenues earned by 11 firms topped market estimates, while six companies reported lower-than-expected revenue. On the EPS front, 12 companies beat wall street estimates and three firms missed, while two companies were in line with the analyst consensus.

The XLRE has gained over 6% year-to-date, compared to the S&P 500’s more than 10% return.

Below are the key quarterly reports from the top three REIT companies this week:

American Tower (AMT): The company beat market expectation in Q3, reflecting solid leasing demand for its telecommunications infrastructure and an outperforming data centers segment. The REIT posted Q3 adjusted FFO per share of $2.87, beating the Visible Alpha consensus of $2.80.  Total operating revenue came in at $2.79B, topping the $2.76B consensus. The REIT raised its full-year guidance, expecting an adjusted FFO per share of $11.04-$11.16, and adjusted EBITDA is expected to be $7.248B-$7.303B.

Vici Properties (VICI): The REIT that invests in casino and entertainment properties posted Q3 adjusted FFO per share of $0.62, in line with the Visible Alpha consensus. Total revenue was $1.07B, beating the $1.06B consensus. Raising the outlook, the company now expects 2026 adjusted FFO per share of $2.47-$2.48 vs. the Visible Alpha consensus of $2.47 and its prior outlook of $2.45-$2.47.

Federal Realty Invs Trust (FRT):  The retail REIT exceeded analyst expectations in Q3 and raised the full-year core FFO guidance to $7.54 to $7.58 from $7.48 to $7.56, above the consensus of $7.55 at the midpoint. In Q3, core FFO per diluted share reached $1.87 from $1.77 in the same period a year ago, above the Visible Alpha consensus of $1.85. Total revenue increased to $339.02M from $322.25M.

For the coming week, 10 REIT stocks are set to report their financial results, of which Realty Income (O), Vivmark Residential (VMRK), Simon Property Group (SPG), and Iron Mountain (IRM) are widely watched.

data.title: Healthcare sector rallies in October amid rotation away from technology stocks
data.description:
Healthcare stocks jumped in October, with the Health Care Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLV) gaining nearly 9.5% as investors rotated out of high-flying technology shares and into defensive sectors such as healthcare, which offer established cash flows.

Healthcare Sector Scorecard

Sector Return: 9.53% month-to-dateBest Performer: Regeneron Pharmaceuticals (+26.28%)Top Detractor: Illumina (-11.19%)

Top healthcare gainers in October

Regeneron Pharmaceuticals (REGN) was the biggest winner in October, gaining 26.3%, as the Eylea maker reported higher-than-expected Q3 2026 results, thanks to approximately 36% YoY revenue growth driven by its collaboration with Sanofi.

It was followed by Charles River Laboratories International (CRL), which jumped 25.3% in October.

Eli Lilly (LLY) surged nearly 23.3% in October on the back of better-than-expected third-quarter results and an increase in its full-year 2026 revenue outlook, driven by strong demand for Mounjaro and Zepbound.

data.title: Earnings scorecard: 21 out of 22 technology companies beat EPS estimates this week
data.description:
Information technology stocks grabbed the spotlight this week as Wall Street digested earnings reports from major companies, including Microsoft (MSFT), Intel (INTC), and Sandisk (SNDK).

The information technology sector (NYSEARCA:XLK) gained nearly 31% so far this year, outperforming about a 13% increase in the broader S&P 500 Index.

In this week's earnings recap, 22 tickers reported results, out of which 21 companies reported earnings beats and 20 beat revenue expectations.

Below are the latest quarterly reports from some key players, which reported results this week:

Microsoft (MSFT) shares rose in extended trading on Wednesday after the Windows maker reported fiscal first-quarter results that topped/missed estimates.

For the period ending Sept. 30, Microsoft said it earned an adjusted $4.89 per share as revenue rose 19% year-over-year (17% in constant currency) to come in at $92.28B. Cloud revenue came in at $63.9B, above the $61.62B estimate. Azure revenue rose 48%, above the estimate of 44.8%.

On the company's earnings call, Microsoft management said it expects fiscal second-quarter revenue to be between $96B and $97.1B, above the $95.63B estimate. 

On the other hand, Intel (INTC) shares plunged 26% in premarket trading on Friday after it issued fourth quarter guidance that missed Wall Street's estimates by a considerable margin.

The semiconductor giant expects its Q4 revenue to be between $15B and $16B, below estimates of $17.05B. Adjusted earnings are forecast to be $0.25 per share, below the $0.43 estimate. Adjusted gross margins are expected to be 38%, below the 42.8% estimate.

Sandisk (SNDK) shares erased initial losses and rose 3% in extended trading on Thursday as the storage maker reported fiscal first-quarter results and guidance that topped Wall Street's forecast by a considerable margin.

Shares have gained more than 380% year-to-date.

For the period ending Oct. 2, Sandisk said it earned an adjusted $49.51 per share as revenue rose 23% year-over-year to come in at $11.03B. Analysts had expected Sandisk to earn an adjusted $46.67 per share on $10.72B in revenue.

Looking ahead to the fiscal second-quarter, Sandisk said it expects to earn between $55 and $57 per share on an adjusted basis, above the $52.60 per share estimate. Sales are forecast to be between $12.2B and $12.6B, with the $12.4B midpoint above the $12.31B estimate.

For the upcoming week, Apple (AAPL), Qualcomm (QCOM), Advanced Micro Devices (AMD), Palantir Technologies (PLTR), and Super Micro Computer (SMCI) are among the key information technology companies that are scheduled to report quarterly results.

data.title: Healthcare Earnings Scoreboard: 96% beat EPS estimates, 70% post Y/Y earnings growth
data.description:
Healthcare companies reported broadly positive Q3 results last week, with every S&P 500 healthcare stock that posted results showing Y/Y topline growth, although earnings growth was less consistent.

Heathcare Earnings Roundup

Bottom Line: Of the 23 companies reporting, 22 firms (96%) exceeded EPS expectations, while 1 fell short. Notably, 16 firms (70%) posted Y/Y earnings growth.

Top Line: Of the 23 companies reporting, 21 firms (91%) exceeded revenue expectations, while 2 fell below analyst estimates. Notably, all 23 firms (100%) posted Y/Y revenue growth.

Let’s take a look at some of the healthcare companies that reported earnings this week:

AbbVie (ABBV) reported Q3 revenue of $17.40B, up 10.3% Y/Y, beating the $17.35B consensus. Adjusted EPS of $3.82 beat the $3.77 estimate. Growth was driven by strong sales of Skyrizi and Rinvoq, which rose 22.7% and 23.9%, respectively. The company raised its FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $13.95–$13.99 from $13.76–$13.96.

Eli Lilly (LLY) reported Q3 revenue of $24.40B, up 39% Y/Y, beating the $22.42B consensus. Adjusted EPS of $7.48 beat the $5.60 estimate. Growth was driven by strong demand for Mounjaro and Zepbound. The company raised its FY2026 revenue outlook to $91B–$92B.

Bristol Myers Squibb (BMY) reported Q3 revenue of $13.07B, up 7% Y/Y, beating consensus, while adjusted EPS of $1.35 topped the $1.09 estimate. Growth was driven by its Growth Portfolio, particularly Eliquis, which generated $4.69B in sales, up 25% Y/Y. The company raised its FY2026 revenue outlook but lowered its adjusted EPS forecast to $6.35–$6.55.

Gilead Sciences (GILD) reported Q3 revenue of $8.30B, up 7% Y/Y, beating the $7.79B consensus. Non-GAAP EPS of $2.55 beat the $2.17 estimate. HIV medicines drove growth, with Biktarvy sales rising 10% to $4.1B. Trodelvy sales increased 42% to $506M. Gilead raised its FY2026 product sales outlook to $31B–$31.3B.

Regeneron Pharmaceuticals (REGN) reported Q3 revenue of $5.12B, up 36% Y/Y, beating the $4.56B consensus. Adjusted EPS of $20.07 beat the $16.25 estimate. Growth was driven by strong sales of Dupixent (up 35%), Eylea HD (up 62%) and Libtayo (up 51%).

Biogen (BIIB) reported Q3 revenue of $2.8B, up 11% Y/Y, beating the $2.63B consensus. Non-GAAP EPS of $2.62 topped the $1.98 estimate. Growth Portfolio revenue surged 49% to $1.26B, while Spinraza sales rose 23% to $461M. The company raised the lower end of its FY2026 adjusted EPS outlook to $12.20.

Illumina (ILMN) reported Q3 revenue of $1.13B, up 4.2% Y/Y. GAAP diluted EPS was $1.43 versus $0.98 a year earlier. Clinical demand and NovaSeq X placements supported growth. The company raised its FY2026 revenue outlook to $4.64B–$4.66B and non-GAAP EPS outlook to $5.40–$5.45.

Earnings next week

For the upcoming week, investors will continue to watch healthcare earnings, including reports from Amgen (AMGN), Pfizer (PFE), Vertex Pharmaceuticals (VRTX), Novo Nordisk (NVO) and others.

Healthcare ETFs: (XLV), (VHT), (IYH), (FHLC), (RYH), (XBI) and (IBB).

data.title: Seven of eight consumer staples companies beat EPS estimates in Q3 2026 earnings week: Earnings scorecard
data.description:
The S&P 500 consumer staples sector (XLP) delivered a largely positive Q3 2026 earnings performance, with Coca-Cola, Altria, and Colgate-Palmolive beating both EPS and revenue expectations, while Mondelez topped EPS estimates but narrowly missed revenue forecasts. 

Eight companies from S&P 500 consumer staples sector reported earnings this week, with seven beating EPS estimates and one reporting in line with expectations. On the revenue front, seven companies topped consensus estimates, while one missed expectations.

Here’s a look at how the major companies performed:

Coca-Cola (KO): Reported adjusted EPS of $0.91, beating estimates by $0.03, while revenue increased 7.2% Y/Y to $13.4B, exceeding expectations by $470M. Strong international demand and 7% organic revenue growth supported results. Management raised its FY2026 comparable EPS growth outlook to at least 11%.

Altria (MO): Posted adjusted EPS of $1.52, up 4.8% Y/Y and $0.01 above estimates. Revenue rose 3.4% Y/Y to $5.44B, beating expectations by $130M. The company raised its FY2026 EPS guidance to $5.66–$5.74 and expanded its share repurchase program by $1B. Shares gained 5% following the results.

Mondelez (MDLZ): Delivered adjusted EPS of $0.78, beating estimates by $0.07, while revenue increased 2.4% Y/Y to $9.97B, missing expectations by $20M. Volume-led growth and improved margins supported earnings. Shares rose 3.5% after the announcement.

Colgate-Palmolive (CL): Reported adjusted EPS of $0.97, beating estimates by $0.04, while revenue grew 4.7% Y/Y to $5.37B, exceeding expectations by $40M. Growth was supported by higher volumes and pricing gains. Management raised its FY2026 adjusted EPS growth outlook to 5%–7%.

Upcomings earnings 

Seven companies from the S&P 500 consumer staples sector are expected to report earnings next week: Estee Lauder (EL), Clorox (CLX), Archer Daniels Midland (ADM), Keurig Dr Pepper (KDP), Sysco (SYY), Kraft Heinz (KHC), and Kimberly-Clark (KMB). The upcoming reporters span personal care, household products, food products, beverages, and food distribution.

data.title: Notable tech headlines for the week: Intel, Microsoft and Sandisk in focus
data.description:
The tech sector remained in the spotlight this week as investors assessed earnings reports from companies including Intel, Microsoft, and Sandisk.

The tech-focused Nasdaq Composite Index (COMP:IND) closed in the red on Friday, with investors selling off technology stocks after discouraging earnings reports. The top S&P 500 technology gainers and losers for the last week are as follows:

Top Gainers:

Gen Digital (GEN) +17.16%

Global Payments (GPN) +16.93%

Flex (FLEX) +12.97%

Lumentum (LITE) +11.18%

NXP Semiconductors (NXPI) +10.62%

Top Losers:

ServiceNow (NOW) -33.87%

F5 (FFIV) -25.71%

Fortinet (FTNT) -24.40%

Intel (INTC) -24.38%

Twilio (TWLO) -21.68%

Here are some of the important technology stories from this week:

Intel crashes on issuing guidance below Wall Street's forecasts

Intel (INTC) shares plunged 26% on Friday after the company issued fourth quarter guidance that missed Wall Street's estimates by a considerable margin.

The semiconductor giant’s revenue rose 21% year-over-year to $16.51B, almost in-line with estimates, while adjusted profit came in at $0.52 per share compared to the consensus of $0.40. 

The company said its guidance includes an impact of roughly $300 million to revenue and 200 basis points to gross margin. It also expects the industry to remain supply-constrained throughout 2027 and into 2028.

Microsoft taps debt markets with $25B bond sale to boost AI

Microsoft (MSFT) priced $25B in senior unsecured debt, launching a massive ten-tranche bond offering to fund capital expenditures, stock buybacks, and general corporate purposes.

This comes after the company’s first quarter fiscal 2027 results demonstrated surging growth from Azure and multiple paths of AI monetization, drew cheers from analysts and investors. The company also said capital spending is expected to top $50B, with spending expected to accelerate in the second half of fiscal 2027. Nonetheless, Microsoft still expects to be free cash flow positive in fiscal 2027.

Oracle (ORCL) too, unveiled plans to raise capital on Wednesday and said it anticipates a return to positive free cash flow in the second half of its 2028 fiscal year.

Sandisk tumbles even as Wall Street praises results

Sandisk (SNDK) was in focus after it reported stronger-than-expected results and guidance and announced a stock split. However, investors seemingly wanted more from the storage company, as shares fell more than 13%.

In addition to the quarterly results, Sandisk said its board of directors has approved an eight-for-one stock split, effective Nov. 19. 

In other news, Apple (AAPL) revealed its new iMac and 14-inch MacBook Pro, both equipped with its new in-house M6 chip, on Tuesday. The company also acquired agentic platform Ascension Labs, the European Commission announced on Friday.

According to a Bloomberg report, Marvell Technology (MRVL) is in advanced discussions to buy data center optics maker Lumentum Holdings (LITE). A deal could happen as soon as next week, the report added.

data.title: Notable analyst calls this week: Broadcom, Moderna and Abbott among top picks
data.description:
The S&P 500 (SP500) closed in the red on Friday, after investors digested corporate results from big companies including Alphabet and Microsoft during the week.

Wall Street analysts issued fresh round of upgrades and downgrades. Here are some of the major calls for the week:

Broadcom gets bullish rating from D.A. Davidson

D.A. Davidson upgraded Broadcom (AVGO) to Buy from Neutral and upped its price target on the stock to $400 from $350.

“Our reading of the Anthropic S1 leads us to believe the IPO will proceed, Anthropic will raise its capital, and next year OpenAI will raise more capital in its own IPO, allowing Broadcom to meet its expectations for the next couple of years,” DA Davidson analyst Gil Luria wrote.

“At the current 16x multiple on 2027 EPS, AVGO is trading as if the chances of that happening are near zero, which creates significant upside if those deals both materialize,” Luria added.

William Blair is latest to downgrade Moderna on valuation

William Blair became the latest brokerage to downgrade Moderna (MRNA) to Market Perform from Outperform., citing valuation concerns following a late-stage win for its cancer shot developed with Merck (MRK).

Noting that Moderna is “up 545% year-to-date and up nearly 250% since the positive INTERPATH-001 trial news announced in August,” William Blair analyst Myles Minter downgraded the stock.

“Although we are incrementally more confident in success given the magnitude of efficacy shown in adjuvant melanoma, development in these additional tumors is not without meaningful clinical and biological risk,” Minter wrote.

Abbott downgraded on guidance cut

Argus Research cut its 12-month rating on Abbott (ABT) to Hold from Buy, citing the company’s recent decision to trim its full-year growth outlook.

With its Q3 2026 results last week, Abbott set its full-year outlook for comparable sales growth at about 6% down from 6.5% - 7.5% previously, an indication of slower growth in its key growth drivers—electrophysiology and diabetes care, according to analyst David Toung.

“The company faces pricing pressure in markets in which it seeks reimbursement coverage for its products,” Toung wrote, adding it also faces tariff-related costs, and “in the near term, it faces operational risks as it seeks to control costs while addressing supply chain issues.”

Jefferies upgrades Rivian to Buy

Jefferies upgraded Rivian (RIVN) to Buy from Hold, saying a recent share-price correction offers an attractive entry point as the electric-vehicle maker makes progress toward positive automotive gross margins and scales up its R2 model.

Analysts led by Philippe Houchois said third-quarter results showed an acceleration toward positive automotive gross margins, while improved delivery and earnings guidance extended a run of positive execution and capital-discipline surprises. 

The brokerage maintained its $17 price target.

GF Securities upped its price target for AMD (AMD) to $720 ahead of its third-quarter results, set to be released on Nov. 3.

“[We] expect inline results but shy in current quarter guidance,” GF analyst Jeff Pu wrote in a note to clients. “We also note that investor expectation on AMD is high. Nevertheless, driven by the trend of agentic AI, we expect the company to reiterate the bullish outlook for its datacenter business in 2027 of well over 100% YoY. We remain bullish, backed by robust server CPU TAM, AMD’s strong server CPU product cycle, recent wafer supply increase and MI450/MI455X re-acceleration.”

Constellium (CSTM) was upgraded by J.P. Morgan to Overweight from Neutral with a $35 price target, following Q3 results, including better-than-expected adjusted EBITDA of $280M, while lifting full-year EBITDA guidance by 5% to $1.03B-$1.06B on solid Automotive Structures & Industry segment demand.

data.title: 3 out of 4 communications services stocks deliver EPS wins this week: Earnings Scorecard
data.description:
Communications services stocks grabbed the spotlight this week as Wall Street digested earnings reports from major names, including Alphabet (GOOG) and Verizon (VZ).

The communications services sector (XLC) lost over 14% so far this year, compared to the nearly 13% rise in the broader S&P 500 Index.

In this week's earnings recap, four tickers reported results, all of which three reported earnings beats. On the revenue side, two companies exceeded revenue expectations, while two companies trailed estimates.

Below are the latest quarterly reports from some key players, which reported results this week:

Alphabet (GOOG) (GOOGL) closed over 12% lower on Thursday following the tech giant’s release of the company's third-quarter financial results, which marked its first quarterly earnings miss since Q4 2022. Q3 earnings trailed Wall Street estimates, despite a more than doubling of Google Cloud revenue as demand for artificial intelligence infrastructure and services surged.

Verizon Communications (VZ) reported third-quarter revenue and adjusted earnings above analysts’ estimates, as well as stronger subscriber additions and higher margins that helped the telecom company lift its full-year 2026 guidance for a third consecutive quarter.

T-Mobile (TMUS) increased the number of new customers and saw higher average revenue per account (ARPA) leading to a 7.4% increase in third-quarter revenue and a 34% improvement in earnings, both of which beat Wall Street’s expectations.

For the upcoming week, Charter Communications (CHTR), Live Nation Entertainment (LYV), Fox (FOX), and News Corp (NWSA) are some communication services names that are scheduled to report quarterly results.
